author: RaccoonNinja
quote:
The game is okay at first, while the story has gotten better compared to the GTAV in terms of the emotional tone and connection between the two main characters. It still didn't feel like a GTA game in terms of gameplay. While I understand games change directions and such. It's not my cup of tea. I've been waiting for this game as everyone else for 13 years. During that wait, I think my preference of gaming has changed. It's obviously not the most complete realistic game, but how much simulating gameplay that they added, this plays more attune to RDR2 with a GTA name over it then a sequel **** game. Visually, it is better than GTAV by a mile. I just don't think the cost is worth to what the game offers. 13 years and its a buggy mess. Early access games, I can understand but Rockstar? Indie companies and eastern game developers have shown that it's possible to develop a game that's fun gameplay, engaging storylines, and the same $40-60 games that people have asked for. The woke stuff that most are talking about, isn't even a big deal. Most successful games, in the past, were technically woke if you look back on it. I think if you enjoy RDR2 style of game, then this will be up your alley. If you're looking for nostalgia in the sense that it's a game in Vice City, and it has the GTA name on it. By all means. But if you're expecting an open-world game, where you can do whatever you want, commit all the heinous act, and wild chaos....well it's kinda there, you just have to be open minded. The game starts off slow, and it slowly opens the world more, but you can't do EVERYTHING, like not every NPC you see will be killable. That doesn't bother me, but I think if that stays the same even until multiplayer comes out, I don't think the chaos seeking gamers will have fun with that. 

TLDR: It's a generally fun game for the first time through from my experience, but the simulating gameplay in terms of getting gas and all these mini-games attached  to some of the actions you do feels like they wanted to cater to the "realism" fan, the honeymoon period fell off. Buggy opening day, for a game developer giant out of Rockstar, and what was delivered, compared to the expectation set by the waiting time. I don't think I can recommend to everybody.
